title: Country, rockabilly, and classics headline 50th annual Gassaway Days | News | wvnews.com
text:
GASSAWAY, W.Va. — Braxton County music lovers will have no shortage of entertainment during the 50th annual Gassaway Days celebration as a diverse lineup of country, rockabilly, gospel and classic hits takes center stage at Kenton Meadows Field.
The festival, scheduled for July 3-4, will not only mark the golden anniversary of Gassaway Days but also serve as part of the community’s celebration of America’s 250th anniversary. Festival organizers have assembled a lineup designed to appeal to multiple generations of music fans, with performances spanning several genres and culminating each evening with a fireworks display.
The live entertainment begins Friday, July 3, at 5:15 p.m. with a performance by the Gassaway Baptist Church Choir and Praise Band, helping set the tone for two days of community celebration.
Later that evening, the Brayden Williamson Band will take the stage from 7 to 8:30 p.m. Williamson has built a reputation as one of the region’s rising traditional country performers, blending original music with crowd-pleasing covers of some of the genre’s most recognizable artists.
His set list regularly features songs from country legends such as Johnny Cash and Merle Haggard while also incorporating selections from artists including Eric Clapton and Jimmy Buffett. Williamson’s growing popularity has been fueled in part by original songs that have gained attention on social media and streaming platforms, helping him reach audiences beyond West Virginia.
Friday night’s headlining performance will begin at 8:45 p.m. with Tane Lynne & Shadow Creek.
The six-piece band offers a mix of traditional country music and classic rock influences, creating a sound that appeals to a broad audience. Drawing inspiration from iconic performers such as Patsy Cline, Waylon Jennings and Creedence Clearwater Revival, the group has become known for energetic live performances that blend familiar favorites with contemporary country sounds.
Festival organizers expect the band’s performance to provide a fitting lead-in to the evening fireworks show.
The music continues Saturday, July 4, with another evening of live entertainment highlighted by two well-known regional acts.
Taking the stage at 7 p.m. will be Cody Clayton Eagle and his band. Eagle, an accomplished country singer-songwriter, earned national attention in 2019 when he received a coveted golden ticket to Hollywood during auditions for ABC’s “American Idol.”
Since his appearance on the nationally televised competition, Eagle has continued building his career while sharing stages with a variety of notable performers. His résumé includes appearances alongside Charles Wesley Godwin, “The Voice” winner Jake Hoot and the rock band Slaughter, among others.
Known for combining traditional country roots with a modern sound, Eagle’s performance is expected to be one of the festival’s marquee attractions.
Closing out the festival’s live entertainment lineup will be the Back in the Day Show Band, which takes the stage at 8:45 p.m. Saturday.
The five-piece group features three vocalists and specializes in a nostalgic “sock hop” style show that encourages audience participation through classic hits and dance favorites spanning multiple decades.
The band made a strong impression during last year’s festival and quickly became one of the standout attractions, according to Gassaway Mayor Paula Cunningham.
“My favorite, at least from last year, was an oldies group called Back in the Day, and they were available,” Cunningham said. “They’re going to be our main attraction on Saturday night. They will be the second act before the fireworks, and they’re coming down from Morgantown. They play all different types of music, and they just were a big hit last year.”
Cunningham said one of the group’s greatest strengths is its ability to connect with audience members of all ages, creating an atmosphere that encourages families to get involved rather than simply watch from their seats.
She recalled numerous examples of crowd participation during the band’s previous appearance, including grandparents, parents and children dancing together throughout the performance.
“Because of the beat and their performance, they get a lot of audience participation, and again, intergenerational,” Cunningham said. “I’m thinking of one woman last year who just basically grabbed hands with her, I assume, great-grandchild, and they’re just twisting and shouting.”
That type of shared experience is exactly what organizers hope to recreate during this year’s milestone celebration.
With a schedule featuring gospel music, traditional country, classic rock influences, nationally recognized performers and nostalgic oldies favorites, festival officials believe the entertainment lineup reflects the broad appeal that has helped Gassaway Days remain a community tradition for five decades.
As residents and visitors gather to celebrate both the festival’s 50th anniversary and America’s Semiquincentennial, organizers expect the music at Kenton Meadows Field to once again serve as one of the event’s biggest draws, bringing together generations of festivalgoers for two evenings of live entertainment, community fellowship and patriotic celebration before the night skies light up with fireworks.
